card.name: Verb after adverse-effect subject
card.fires_on: The verb right after a lab or adverse-event subject in warnings, such as 'has occurred', 'have been observed' or 'occur'. It sits in sections on blood counts, bleeding or electrolytes.

modes.label: Occurred / have been
modes.description: Auxiliary or main verb after a side-effect noun phrase, starting a report statement.
modes.example: Gastrointestinal and intracerebral hemorrhage has<< occurred>> during thrombocytopenia in

modes.label: Decreases/elevations phrase
modes.description: Linking word or verb after a noun like decreases or elevations of a lab value.
modes.example: Hypotension: Decreases<< in>> blood pressure associated with diltiazem

card.writes: It seems to push toward generic hedged-frequency phrasing like 'typical' or 'generally', and away from 'possibly' or 'potentially'.
card.plain: It marks the verb that says a side effect or lab change was seen or reported in patients.
